evidence_summary: Tone Machines identifies the Nomad Banshee as made by Applied and describes the same Banshee as an Applied-branded fuzz. Effects Database separately records an Applied Banshee Fuzz and a Nomad-branded state; the exact first-production date remains approximate.
Tone Machines states the Nomad Banshee was made by Applied Audio and appeared around 1968; Effects Database documents the Nomad (by Applied) Banshee as the marketed version.

model_or_family: Panther Box Fuzz-Tone and Treble Boost
evidence_summary: Tone Machines' 2025 reconstruction argues that Goya effects after 1966 were made in the U.S. by Applied Audio, specifically identifying the Panther Box and citing matching construction details; Kitrae independently places the Panther in the 1967 Goya catalog and notes it may be the same platform as Applied's fuzz.

Tone Machines places the Goya Fury Box among the additional Applied effects added to the Goya lineup in 1968; Kitrae notes that the Goya Fury may share the Panther/Applied fuzz circuit. Exact factory identity is retained as research-level rather than treated as a direct catalog manufacturer statement.

The 1968 Goya catalog explicitly says the Boom Box was made in U.S.A.; Tone Machines identifies the Boom Box as one of the Applied effects added to Goya's lineup in 1968, so Applied remains a strong but separately documented OEM reconstruction.

Effects Database identifies Applied Big Bass as a late-1960s U.S. bass-booster state and links it to Goya Boom Box and Conrad Bass Hawk. The broader family relationship is useful, but the database's Applied Electronics naming differs from the Applied Audio Products naming used in the Tone Machines reconstruction.

Effects Database links Conrad Bass Hawk to the Applied Big Bass / Goya Boom Box family. Because the available evidence is family-level rather than a direct surviving factory document, the builder attribution remains research-only.

A cross-check confirms the Rogue remains distinct from the Banshee despite shared Applied/Nomad enclosure lineage. Tone Machines describes the Rogue as following the Nomad Banshee and using the same basic family with an additional gain stage, while Effects Database documents the separate Applied Rogue model.
